title: Building a family verification protocol
body_md:
## Make a family plan that survives panic

A family verification plan is a short agreement made *before* an urgent call. Its purpose is not to identify every deepfake. It gives everyone permission to pause, disconnect and check through a route chosen in advance. The FTC describes fake emergency callers who exploit urgency, secrecy, personal details and sometimes a cloned voice. The same plan helps if the caller simply imitates a voice or uses a stolen phone.

Start with two or three people likely to receive an emergency request. Agree on three rules: no money or account codes on an incoming call; call the person back on a saved number; if there is no answer, contact another relative or a real institution through its published number. Decide who can help a young or older relative make that second call. Rehearse a short sentence: “I want to help. I am hanging up and calling you on the number I already have.” A real emergency can still be handled promptly.

An optional shared phrase is a reminder, not proof. Choose one unrelated to public birthdays or pet names; do not reuse a password or one-time account code. Keep the circle small, explain when to use it, and replace it if exposed. A caller who knows the phrase still needs a callback; a real person who forgets it still deserves a welfare check. If no phrase is practical, the callback plan remains useful. Do not impose a fixed renewal date as if rotation alone made it safe.

Write down the route in a safe place: saved contact numbers, a second family contact, and locally relevant emergency numbers. Do not put secret phrases in a shared public post. During a call, one person can handle the independent callback while another stays ready to seek medical or police help. Afterward, tell the family what happened without shaming the person who received the call. If money was sent, promptly ask the bank or payment provider about available recovery and use local reporting channels.

The plan works only if the people who may receive a call know it and have practised it. Spend a few minutes rehearsing the disconnect-and-callback step rather than trying to make everyone an audio-forensics expert.

widget_config.goal: Agree and practise a family callback plan for urgent requests, with a safe fallback when someone is unreachable.
widget_config.today_action: Ask two close people to practise the sentence “I will call you back on your saved number,” and save a backup contact.
widget_config.scope: General household education, checked 20 October 2026; adapt emergency contacts and payment recovery to your country. A shared phrase is optional, not an authentication guarantee.

sources.title: FTC: Scammers Use Fake Emergencies To Steal Your Money
sources.scope: US consumer advice, September 2023; voice cloning, urgency, independent callback and another relative. The US reporting route is jurisdiction-specific.

blocks.title: A “granddaughter” asks to hide a payment
blocks.situation: A synthetic caller says she is your granddaughter, has been detained, and needs a payment through a new intermediary before anyone else hears.
blocks.analysis: The secrecy rule is designed to disable the family network. End the call, use the saved number and the agreed backup person. If a real detention is possible, independently contact the relevant local authority; do not pay the caller’s intermediary.

blocks.title: A real relative forgets the phrase
blocks.situation: Synthetic example: After an injury, your uncle calls from a clinic’s phone. He cannot remember the optional family phrase and wants someone to collect him, not transfer money.
blocks.analysis: A missing phrase does not make him a fraudster. Call the clinic using its published number or another relative to check the location, then arrange help. The protocol should support care, not block it.

blocks.title: Build the family response
blocks.setup: Synthetic scenario: three relatives are agreeing how to handle an urgent call; one uses an older phone and one travels often.

steps.prompt: What is the rule for an incoming money request?

choices.text: End the call and dial the saved number yourself
choices.consequence: Everyone has a simple first move.
choices.explanation: A saved contact exists outside the caller’s story.

choices.text: Ask the caller to text a proof photo
choices.consequence: A convincing image arrives, but identity remains unverified.
choices.explanation: The caller controls the image as well as the call.

steps.prompt: The traveller may be unreachable. Choose the fallback.

choices.text: Call a second agreed relative or published institution
choices.consequence: The plan still works without one phone.
choices.explanation: Independent welfare checks are possible without sending money to the caller.

choices.text: Assume no answer confirms the emergency payment
choices.consequence: An unreachable phone turns into false “evidence.”
choices.explanation: No answer can have many ordinary causes.

steps.prompt: A relative proposes a shared phrase. How should it be used?

choices.text: As sole proof, replacing the callback
choices.consequence: One overheard phrase can defeat the whole plan.
choices.explanation: A shared secret alone does not verify the current situation.

choices.text: As an optional clue alongside independent callback
choices.consequence: The phrase helps memory without becoming a master key.
choices.explanation: It can leak or be forgotten; the saved route remains primary.

blocks.debrief: The agreed action is a short, rehearsed callback with a fallback. A phrase can help but cannot override the callback. Revisit the choices together as a family.

questions.prompt: A real relative forgets the family phrase during an injury.

choices.text: Refuse all help because the phrase is missing
choices.explanation: A phrase is optional and fallible.

choices.text: Verify through a clinic or another saved contact, then help
choices.explanation: The plan supports a genuine emergency without treating memory failure as guilt.

questions.prompt: Who should know the response plan?

choices.text: Only the person who designed it
choices.explanation: Others need to practise before panic.

choices.text: People likely to receive or verify an urgent request
choices.explanation: The callback fails if only one family member knows it.

questions.prompt: A caller supplies a hospital phone number. What do you do?

choices.explanation: A number supplied by the caller can lead to an accomplice.

choices.text: Call it and treat the answer as independent proof
choices.explanation: The source of the number is still the unverified caller.
